text: Fischer and Ravizza argue that moral responsibility requires guidance control rather than regulative control. Guidance control is:
choices: acting from one's own, moderately reasons-responsive mechanism, whether or not alternatives are open.
the ability to do otherwise, to take a genuinely different path, preserved even under determinism.
an agent-causal power to originate action independently of prior events.
the mesh between one's first-order desires and second-order volitions.
explanation: Fischer and Ravizza concede that determinism removes regulative control (the ability to do otherwise) but argue responsibility needs only guidance control: ownership of a moderately reasons-responsive mechanism. Regulative control is precisely what they deny is necessary; the mesh is Frankfurt's account and agent-causation is libertarian.
